newsitem.title: USA: Prices for U.S. insurance deals up in H1 '97.
newsitem.headline: Prices for U.S. insurance deals up in H1 '97.

text.p: The average price of U.S. insurance mergers rose in the first half of 1997 as industry consolidation continued at a record-setting pace, research firm SNL Securities said.

So far in 1997, the median price/earnings multiple for life and health deals was 15.3 compared with a price/earnings multiple of 14.3 for all of 1996, SNL's Insurance Mergers & Acquisitions newsletter said in a statement about its mid-year industry review.
The average price of property-casualty deals, which are usually valued using price/book value, also rose in the first half of 1997, SNL said.
The median price/book value of property and casualty deals in the first-half of 1997 rose to 188.7 percent from 130 percent a year ago.
However, the median price/earnings multiple for property and casualty transactions fell to 10.3 from 14.8 last year.
"The general consensus in the industry is that people are starting to pay more," Mark Kilduff, an analyst for Insurance Mergers & Acquisitions said in a telephone interview.
Meanwhile, the pace of consolidation continued to be red hot, with 104 deals valued at $16.5 billion announced in the first half of 1997, SNL said.
The total deal value for mergers of life, health, property-casualty, and broker/agency companies for all of 1996 totaled $21.8 billion, SNL said.
"We've seen companies of all sizes divesting non-core businesses and strengthening existing product lines either by buying a portfolio or an operating company," Kilduff said in a statement.
"We believe the industry is only now at the beginning of a long-term push toward consolidation," he said.
Wall Street also has profited from the consolidation push.
Goldman, Sachs & Co advised on eight insurance acquisitions valued at $8.4 billion in the first six months of 1997, putting it in the top spot in SNL's industrywide survey.
Morgan, Stanley, Dean Witter, Discover & Co., which advised on 11 deals valued at $5.8 billion, ranked second.
The top insurance merger and acquisition law firm was Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom, with six deals valued at $5.7 billion.
"Many of the big players in the insurance industry have developed the expertise to effectively acquire and integrate their targets," SNL Securities Principal John Racine said in a statement.
"As they've grown, they've gone after larger companies. Now a class of highly efficient and experienced buyers stands ready to drive consolidation well into 1998 and beyond," he said.
